newsitem.title: USA: Power still out for 400,000 in snowy New England.
newsitem.headline: Power still out for 400,000 in snowy New England.

text.p: One day after an early spring blizzard buried parts of New England under three feet of snow, some 400,000 people remained without power, state officials said Wednesday.

The storm's effects continued to hamper travel in the region despite beautiful, clear skies and temperatures that were expected to reach into the 50s. Major highways were for the most part clear, but most secondary roads in the region remained clogged.

Boston's Logan International Airport was operating with just one runway Wednesday morning. The airport had hoped to be fully operational by then, but the 25.4 inches of heavy, wet snow proved too much for the ploughs. High winds, with gusts higher than 50 mph, whipped the airport.
Many airlines cancelled flights and officials estimated some passengers would not get to their destinations before Friday.
Mass transit in the region was also recovering, though commuter rail service in Connecticut and Massachusetts reported delays of up to an hour.
A state of emergency remained in effect for a second day in Massachusetts and most of the state's schools, from day care centres to universities, remained closed.
The blizzard wiped out power to blue collar towns like Lynn and Lowell northeast of Boston as well as to the tony resort island of Martha's Vineyard.

Massachusetts utilities called in hundreds of extra crews from as far away as Maryland, Pennsylvania, Maine and Canada to work on the downed power lines. Massachusetts Emergency Management Agency spokesmen said some 78,500 customers remained without power in the state. The affected areas included Cape Cod and Martha's Vineyard as well as the south shore.
Connecticut's emergency agency reported 29,000 customers were still without power.
